# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The user's request, verbatim:

> I want to create a completely new design. Intended to visually assist with structuring frontend application development by identifying and linking:
>
> * UI windows/pages and components => "UI Element"
> * Input fields / Data elements  => "Data Element"
> * Actions/interactions => "Action".
> * Background Processes and Functions => "Function"
>
> The name for this kind of visualization should be called a "Functional Decomposition Graph", with as file type the extension .fdg.
>
> Each visualization of this kind is able to show all of the above elements at the same time. And provides bezier curve based line drawing capabilities between the elements.
> The rules wrt what is allowed to be drawn to what is as per below:
>
> * A UI Element can be linked to:
>    * One or more UI Element (as children)
>    * One or more Actions => As children (to for example represent a button click).
>    * One or more Data Elements => e.g. to represent fields in a UI, or an object that is bound to a UI, or a collection of objects that are shown in a list.
>    * One or more Functions => e.g. background processes or important code functions that relate to the UI Element.
> * A Data Element can be linked to:
>    * One or more Data Elements => As child properties of an object. This can be done nesting.
>    * One action element => As a child data property of that action process.
>    * One UI element => as a child data property used by the UI element.
> * An Action element can be linked to:
>    * One or more Functions => E.g. to represent background processes or important code functions that relate to the action.
>    * One UI Element => E.g. to represent that a new page is shown, or that a UI element should be updated.
> * A background process can be linked to:
>    * A UI element => As a child.
>    * A action element => As a child.
>    * A data element => as a child.
> * A comment element that cannot be linked to anything.
>
> For the elements the following vlsuals should be used:
>
> * UI Element
>    * A Superellipse.
>    * With hex color #aaed92
>    * Width can be changed by dragging its border.
>    * Height is constant and same as all other elements.
> * Data Element
>    * A parallelogram with top shifted right relative to bottom.
>    * With hex color #ededed
>    * Width can be changed by dragging its border.
>    * Height is constant and same as all other elements.
> * Action
>    * A trapezoid with smaller bottom then top.
>    * With hex color #9edcfa
>    * Width can be changed by dragging its border.
>    * Height is constant and same as all other elements.
> * Background process / function:
>    * A 'diode', a element based on the left side as square lines and the right side ellipsoid/circular. Just a fill color and a border. No other ornaments.
>    * With hex color #86e6d9
>    * Width can be changed by dragging its border.
>    * Height is constant and same as all other elements.
> * Comment
>    * A resizable, multiline box with automatic text wrapping.
>    * With hex color #fcf281
>    * Both width and height can be changed.
>
> Also:
>
> * All elements can be linked using one side arrowed bezier curve connectors.
> * All elements can be dragged and dropped from the toolbox.
> * Connectors can also be drawn.
> * Connections can be given a name in the property grid, when given it is also shown in the visual diagram.
> * All elements and connectors have a property called Description that can also be added in the property grid, but is never shown on the diagram.
>
> Always use standard conventions and centralized code wherever possible. Make a plan for this.

### The user's rulings on what the request left open

The request's text left real choices open, and they change the rules. They were put to the user as selections on 2026-09-15, and these are the user's answers. Four of them differ from the recommendation offered, and that is recorded beside each.

| Question | The user's ruling |
| --- | --- |
| Which way do arrows point? | **Parent to child.** "X linked to Y as a child" names one link type, whichever end the sentence starts from. |
| What does "one" mean for a Data Element? | **A Data Element has at most one parent in total**, among UI Element, Action and Data Element. |
| "A background process can be linked to a UI element, an action, a data element, as a child" | **The Function is the child** in all three. That adds a Data Element to Function link, which the Data Element list does not name. |
| Links the text does not mention | **Function to Function is allowed**, as a call chain. Action to Action, and every other unlisted pair, is refused. *(The recommendation offered was to refuse all unlisted pairs.)* |
| Action to "one UI Element" | **At most one outgoing Action to UI Element link per Action.** |
| How many parents may an Action or a Function have? | **Both at most one.** An Action has at most one parent UI Element; a Function has at most one parent in total, among UI Element, Action, Data Element and Function. **So a background process shared by several parents is not expressible.** *(The recommendation offered was to let a Function have several parents.)* |
| Cycles in parent to child links | **Blocked while drawing:** a link that would close a cycle is never offered or highlighted. *(The recommendation offered was to report cycles as problems rather than block them.)* |
| Which links the cycle rule covers | **Ownership links only: UI child, Action, Data and Function. Action to UI Element (Shows) is exempt**, so navigating back to a page, and an Action updating its own page, can be drawn, while ownership stays loop-free. **This replaces an earlier ruling** that the rule covered every link. That earlier answer was given on a consequence stated incompletely - *"a button can never update or navigate to its own page or any page above it"* - which omitted that covering every link also blocks round-trip navigation, such as a task list to a task detail and back. Asked again with that consequence stated, the user chose ownership links only, which was the recommendation. |
| Comments and links | **Not offered at all:** a Comment has no anchors, starts and ends no connection, and is never highlighted. |
| Editing a Comment's text | **Both** in the property grid and in place, with a new shared multiline inline editor; both edit the same text. |
| Element names | **A Name is drawn inside every shape except the Comment**, editable in place and in the property grid. |
| Example data | **Hand-authored, on a given subject**: *"create an example based on the workflow of a mobile application that helps field service employees tick of their planning and per-task steps."* Exempt from the published-data rule, with the reason recorded. |
| Catalog origin tag | **`etalii/functional-decomposition-graph`.** *(The recommendation offered was `generic/functional-decomposition-graph`.)* |
| How many parents may a child UI Element have? | **At most one parent UI Element.** |
| Colours | **Five theme tokens: the user's hex exactly in light mode, darker variants of each hue in dark mode, with light label text on the dark fills.** *(This is the recommended option; the preference offered within it was the same hex in both modes.)* |

**Nothing is still open.** Every choice above is the user's.

**"Standard conventions and centralized code wherever possible" is the user's own requirement, and it decides the shape of this specification.** The diagram is built as a declarative module on the shared canvas library, where the only module code is event handlers for actions and validation. **Where the library cannot express something the user asked for, that is a finding that the library lacks a capability, recorded here as library work, never a module exception** (`declarative-diagram-modules`).

## What was measured

The shared canvas library, read at `develop` `59f1ed3a` on 2026-09-15, against each capability the request needs.

| Capability | State | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Width-only border-drag resize | **Exists** | `sizing: "user"` earns left and right handles (`DiagramCanvas.tsx`), raising `element-resized` with a `side` of `left` or `right`. Only `timeline` uses it. No declared shared height. |
| Width **and** height resize | **Missing** | Handles, resize state and `resizedBounds` are left/right only. |
| Wrapped multiline text | **Missing** | `LabelRule.wrap` is declared and **read by nothing**: a field that silently does nothing. Its successor `LabelDeclaration` has no wrap. |
| Multiline inline editing | **Missing** | `InlineLabelEditor` is a single-line input, and editing is refused on multi-line labels. |
| Parallelogram, top shifted right | **Exists** | Built-in `parallelogram`, corners `[0.2,0] [1,0] [0.8,1] [0,1]`: exactly the lean asked for. |
| Superellipse, trapezoid, diode | **Missing** | Not in `BUILT_IN_SHAPES`; `CustomShapeRef` is forbidden to modules (`declarativeModules` guard). |
| Connection name labels | **Exists** | `RelationTypeDefinition.label` (source, midpoint or target; `editable`) and `DiagramModelConnection.label`. |
| A property in the grid that is never drawn | **Exists** | The grid is the backend's `IContextPropertyProvider`; `c4`, `dotnet-dependency-graph` and `helm-charts` already expose a `Description`. Never drawn means not bound in the definition. |
| Toolbox drag and drop | **Exists** | `ToolboxDefinition`, `onElementDropped` (seven modules), and the drop hold. |
| Declared connection rules driving the valid-target highlight | **Exists, with cardinality** | `endpoints { source, target, allowSelf, cardinality { maxFromSource, maxIntoTarget } }`, checked by the connect gesture. One relation type per source and target pair expresses a full rules table. **No cycle detection** beyond `allowSelf`. |
| One-sided arrowed bezier | **Exists** | `route: "cubic-bezier"`, `endMarker`, markers oriented along the route's tangent. |
| A link that would close a cycle, refused while drawing | **Missing** | The connect gesture checks element types, `allowSelf` and cardinality, and nothing about the path a link would complete. |
| At most one parent across several parent types | **Exists, by declaration shape** | An endpoint's `elementTypes` is a list, so every link into a Data Element can be one relation type with three source types and `maxIntoTarget: 1`. No cross-relation cardinality is needed. |

So the library work is exactly five items: **three shapes, height resize, wrapped text, a multiline editor, and declared cycle prevention** (Requirement 9). Everything else the request needs is already a declaration.

## Alignment with Product Vision

`product.md`'s **"Don't reinvent, integrate"** and `structure.md`'s requirement that a new diagram type add no core code are what the user's "centralized code wherever possible" asks for in their own words. A new notation is the case where hand-rolling is most tempting, because nothing exists to copy, and so it is where the declarative rule is tested hardest.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1 — A declarative module

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the functional decomposition graph built from declarations on the shared library, so that it draws, selects, drags and connects exactly like every other diagram.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the module's client is written THEN it SHALL consist of a registration, a stream hook, a `DiagramDefinition`, and event handlers that answer the library's events through the module's own transport. It SHALL contain no rendering, gesture, selection or label code.
2. IF a behaviour the user asked for cannot be declared THEN it SHALL be added to the shared library under Requirement 9, and SHALL NOT be written in the module.
3. WHEN the module is complete THEN every guard that walks module clients SHALL pass against it unchanged.

### Requirement 2 — The `.fdg` file

**User Story:** As an author, I want my graph stored in a readable text file that survives being edited outside ADP.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a graph is saved THEN it SHALL be written to a body file with the extension `.fdg`, registered by an `.adp` file carrying the type's origin line, in the repository's line-oriented style: a version header line, then elements and connections as indented entries, as `.tml` and `.dgr` are.
2. WHEN a document is read THEN the parser SHALL never throw. What it does not understand SHALL be passed over and survive, and a document that breaks the rules of Requirement 5 SHALL still open, with each breach reported by the validator.
3. WHEN ADP did not change a document THEN it SHALL be written back byte-identical: comments, blank lines, indentation, line endings and a missing final newline included. The fixtures SHALL be byte-compared, and `.gitattributes` SHALL carry `*.fdg -text`.
4. WHEN an element or connection changes THEN only the lines that change SHALL be rewritten, through core's `LineSplice`.
5. WHEN the type is registered THEN its `IDiagramDocumentFactory` SHALL produce an empty, valid document.

### Requirement 3 — Positions are authored

**User Story:** As an author, I want elements to stay where I put them.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an element is dragged THEN its position SHALL be written to the document through a command. Positions SHALL be the author's, never computed.
2. WHEN an element's width is changed THEN the width SHALL be written to the document. WHEN a comment's width or height is changed THEN both SHALL be.
3. WHEN snap applies THEN it SHALL follow the library's snap as it stands when this is implemented. The leading-edge semantics in progress SHALL NOT be restated here, and the implementation SHALL read them from the code.

### Requirement 4 — The five element types

**User Story:** As an author, I want each kind of element to be recognisable at a glance by its shape and colour.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a UI Element is drawn THEN it SHALL be a superellipse; a Data Element a parallelogram with its top shifted right relative to its bottom; an Action a trapezoid narrower at the bottom than the top; a Function a diode, square on the left and round on the right, with only a fill and a border; and a Comment a box.
2. WHEN a UI Element, Data Element, Action or Function is drawn THEN all four SHALL share one height, and each SHALL have its own width, changeable by dragging its left or right border.
3. WHEN a Comment is drawn THEN both its width and its height SHALL be changeable, and its text SHALL wrap automatically within the box across as many lines as it needs.
4. WHEN any element's text is drawn THEN it SHALL stay inside its shape - within the shape's own outline, not merely its bounding box, since a trapezoid's and a parallelogram's corners are empty. **Text escaping its shape is a repeated defect class in this repository** (`databricks`, `c4`, `shacl`), so this criterion SHALL be checked in a real browser for every shape at the shared height, at a minimum and a generous width, and for a Comment with more text than fits.
5. WHEN colours are applied THEN each element type's fill SHALL be a theme token defined in both modes, per the user's ruling - never a literal in the module's stylesheet. The tokens follow the theme's existing diagram token, `--color-diagram-potential`: `--color-diagram-fdg-ui-element`, `--color-diagram-fdg-data-element`, `--color-diagram-fdg-action`, `--color-diagram-fdg-function` and `--color-diagram-fdg-comment`. **In light mode each SHALL be exactly the user's hex** - `#aaed92`, `#ededed`, `#9edcfa`, `#86e6d9` and `#fcf281` - and **in dark mode a darker variant of the same hue**.
6. WHEN text is drawn on a fill THEN it SHALL use the theme's `--color-text`, which is dark in the light theme and light in the dark theme. **The contrast between that text and each fill SHALL be at least 4.5:1 (WCAG 2.x AA for normal-size text) in both modes**, and the dark variants SHALL be chosen to meet it with a margin, so that rounding cannot take a fill below the line. This is checked by computing each ratio, not by eye. Measured for this specification: the user's light fills already give 12 to 15 to 1; the lightest same-hue dark variants that reach 4.5 to 1 against the dark theme's text are `#318015`, `#707070`, `#0977ac`, `#1a7e70` and `#7c7203`, sitting at 4.50 to 4.52 to 1, which is too close to the line to adopt unchanged. The design fixes the final values.

### Requirement 5 — Which links may be drawn

**User Story:** As an author, I want the canvas to let me draw only the links the notation allows, and to show me where a link would be accepted before I release it.

#### The rules

| Relation | Parent (source) | Child (target) | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UI child | UI Element | UI Element | A UI Element may have any number of UI children. **A UI Element has at most one parent UI Element** (`maxIntoTarget: 1`). |
| Action | UI Element | Action | A UI Element may have any number of Actions. **An Action has at most one parent** (`maxIntoTarget: 1`). |
| Data | UI Element, Action or Data Element | Data Element | A parent may have any number of Data Elements, nesting included. **A Data Element has at most one parent in total** (one relation type, `maxIntoTarget: 1`). |
| Function | UI Element, Action, Data Element or Function | Function | A parent may have any number of Functions, Function to Function chains included. **A Function has at most one parent in total** (one relation type, `maxIntoTarget: 1`). |
| Shows | Action | UI Element | **An Action shows or updates at most one UI Element** (`maxFromSource: 1`). A UI Element may be shown by any number of Actions: the request sets no limit there, and none was ruled. |

**Refused**, and never highlighted: Action to Action, every pair not listed, and any link to or from a Comment. **No relation allows a link from an element to itself.** One consequence of the one-parent rulings is stated here so it is not rediscovered as a bug: **a background process shared by several parents cannot be drawn; each parent needs its own Function.**

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the rules are declared THEN they SHALL be exactly the five relation types in the table above, every arrow pointing from parent to child, and a link the table does not list SHALL NOT be drawable.
2. WHEN a connection is being drawn THEN the valid-target highlight SHALL be decided by the declarations alone - the relation types, their cardinality and the cycle rule of criterion 4 - through the library's constraint check, with no module code deciding what may connect.
3. WHEN a Comment is on the canvas THEN it SHALL have no anchors, so no connection can start or end on it and it is never highlighted as a target.
4. WHEN a connection is being drawn THEN a target that would close a cycle SHALL NOT be offered or highlighted. The rule SHALL be **declared**, naming the relation types it covers - **UI child, Action, Data and Function, and not Shows** - and SHALL compose with the others as **three independent checks that must all pass**: the target's type is allowed, the cardinality limits are not reached, and the link closes no cycle among the named relation types. None of the three weakens or reorders another. **Because Shows is exempt, an Action may show or update its own page or any page above it, and a navigation loop - a task list, a task detail, and back to the task list - can be drawn.** The one-parent limits alone do not prevent an ownership loop - a Data Element that owns another which owns it back has one parent each - so it is the cycle rule that keeps ownership loop-free; together they make ownership a set of strict trees.
5. WHEN a document breaks a rule, because it was edited outside ADP THEN it SHALL still open, and the validator SHALL report each breach - a forbidden pair, a second parent, a second Shows, a cycle among ownership links - to the Errors and Warnings panel, naming the elements involved.

### Requirement 6 — Connections

**User Story:** As an author, I want links drawn as one-way curves, and named when a name helps.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a connection is drawn THEN it SHALL be a cubic bezier with an arrowhead at one end only, following the curve's direction where it meets the element.
2. WHEN a connection has a name THEN the name SHALL be drawn beside the curve. WHEN it has none THEN nothing SHALL be drawn.
3. WHEN a connection is drawn from the toolbox or by dragging from an element's anchor THEN it SHALL be created through a command, and removing it SHALL be a command with an inverse.

### Requirement 7 — Properties

**User Story:** As an author, I want to record what an element or link means without cluttering the picture.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an element or a connection is selected THEN the property grid SHALL offer a **Description**, for all five element types and every connection, and a Description SHALL NEVER be drawn on the canvas.
2. WHEN a connection is selected THEN the property grid SHALL offer its **Name** (Requirement 6.2).
3. WHEN a UI Element, Data Element, Action or Function is selected THEN the property grid SHALL offer its **Name**, which is drawn inside its shape and SHALL also be editable in place through the shared inline editor. A Comment has no Name; its text is its content (Requirement 9.4).
4. WHEN a property is changed THEN the change SHALL be a command with an inverse, written to the document.

### Requirement 8 — Toolbox and commands

**User Story:** As an author, I want to build a graph from the toolbox and undo anything I do.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the toolbox is shown for this diagram THEN it SHALL offer the five element types, described by the backend as data, and each SHALL be draggable onto the canvas, where dropping it creates the element at the drop position through a command. The drop hold SHALL apply as for every diagram.
2. WHEN a user edits a graph THEN every change SHALL be a command with an inverse, offered through the context-action provider: add and delete an element, move it, change its width (and a Comment's height), connect and disconnect, rename, and set a Description. Undo SHALL restore exactly the lines the change rewrote.
3. WHEN the backend refuses a command THEN the user SHALL see the refusal's sentence, and the document SHALL be unchanged.

### Requirement 9 — The library work this diagram needs

**User Story:** As a maintainer of the shared library, I want capabilities this diagram needs added once, for every module, rather than hand-rolled in one.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the library gains the shapes THEN `BUILT_IN_SHAPES` SHALL include a **superellipse**, a **trapezoid** narrower at the bottom than the top, and a **diode**, square on the left and round on the right. Each SHALL be named for its geometry and never for this diagram, and each SHALL expose the region inside which text fits (Requirement 4.4).
2. WHEN an element type declares that its height may be changed THEN the library SHALL offer top and bottom resize handles, and `element-resized` SHALL name the edge that moved. A type that allows only width SHALL keep today's behaviour exactly, and `timeline` SHALL be unaffected.
3. WHEN a label declares wrapping THEN the library SHALL wrap its text across lines within the space the shape offers. The existing `LabelRule.wrap`, which today does nothing, SHALL either be implemented by this or removed, never left declared and unread.
4. WHEN multiline text is declared editable THEN the library SHALL offer a **shared multiline inline editor**, placed over the text's region and committing through the same event path as today's single-line editor. A Comment's text SHALL be editable both there and in the property grid, and both SHALL edit the same value.
5. WHEN a definition declares a **cycle rule** naming relation types THEN the connect gesture SHALL refuse, and not highlight, any target that would close a directed cycle through links of those types. It SHALL be one declaration beside the relation types, never a module check, and SHALL apply to any diagram that declares it.
6. WHEN any of these is added THEN it SHALL be proven by a library test that was seen to fail before the change, and no module name SHALL appear in its declaration.

### Requirement 10 — Inherited behaviour stays inherited

**User Story:** As a user moving between diagrams, I want this one to behave as the others do.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN elements and connections are selected THEN selection SHALL be the library's, as `centralized-selection` defines it. **This specification SHALL NOT define what "selected" looks like.** That look is `centralized-selection`'s, and is being amended while this is written.
2. WHEN a label is renamed in place, an element is dropped from the toolbox, or a connection's arrowhead is drawn THEN the shared inline rename, the drop hold and the tangent-following markers SHALL apply unchanged.

### Requirement 11 — Examples

**User Story:** As a reader, I want example graphs to open and explore.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN examples are provided THEN they SHALL be **hand-authored**, on the subject the user gave: *"the workflow of a mobile application that helps field service employees tick of their planning and per-task steps."* The notation is new, so no published corpus can exist, and **the examples readme SHALL say so as the reason for exempting them from the published-data rule**, per the user's ruling.
2. WHEN the example is written THEN it SHALL exercise every element type, every allowed relation - Function to Function and nested Data Elements included - at least one named connection, Descriptions on elements and connections, and a Comment. **It SHALL show a round trip of navigation - task list, open task, task detail, back, task list - which the cycle ruling exists to allow.** Its readme SHALL state what it does not demonstrate.
3. WHEN examples are provided THEN they SHALL be seeded into the combined `src/examples/` project like every other module's, and every example's registration SHALL open against the deployed catalog, as `ExampleRegistrationTests` checks for every module.
4. WHEN the example is opened THEN it SHALL break none of Requirement 5's rules; the validator SHALL report nothing for it.

### Requirement 12 — Catalog and documentation

**User Story:** As a reader of the diagram catalog, I want to find this type and its state.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN this specification is approved THEN `docs/diagrams.md` SHALL carry a row for the Functional Decomposition Graph, marked 📝 specified, with origin `etalii/functional-decomposition-graph` per the user's ruling, and the row SHALL move with the type's state thereafter. The same origin SHALL be the `.adp` registration's MIME line and the client registration's mime match.
2. WHEN the module is implemented THEN any touch point it moves in `docs/creating-a-diagram-module.md` SHALL be updated in the same change, and each library capability of Requirement 9 SHALL be documented where module authors are pointed for the definition.
3. WHEN the tasks document is written THEN every acceptance criterion here SHALL be claimed by a task, established by diffing the two sets before the tasks card is raised.

### Requirement 13 — The browser confirms what jsdom cannot

**User Story:** As the user, I want the shapes, colours and text checked where they are seen.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work completes THEN a `tests.md` entry SHALL cover, in a real browser: all five shapes in both themes; text staying inside each shape (Requirement 4.4); width resize on the four and width and height on a Comment; drawing each allowed link, being refused each forbidden one, a second parent and a link that would close a cycle, with no highlight on any refused target; a connection name appearing and disappearing; and a Description never appearing.
2. THEN jsdom SHALL NOT be taken as evidence of any of these, since it applies no CSS and lays out no text.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- The module adds declarations, event handlers and validation, and nothing else (Requirement 1).
- Library additions are named for geometry and behaviour, never for this diagram (Requirement 9.1).

### Reliability

- A document that breaks the rules still opens (Requirement 2.2); a document ADP did not change comes back byte-identical (Requirement 2.3).

### Usability

- The canvas refuses a forbidden link before it is released, not after (Requirement 5.2).

## Sources

- The user's request, quoted verbatim above, and the user's rulings on its open questions, given as selections on 2026-09-15.
- The shared canvas library at `develop` `59f1ed3a`: `diagramDefinition.ts`, `diagramEvents.ts`, `DiagramCanvas.tsx`, `labels.ts`, `InlineLabelEditor.tsx`, and the `declarativeModules` guard.
- `tech.md`, *Specifying a diagram type*; `docs/creating-a-diagram-module.md`; the `.tml`, `.dgr` and `.cld` example documents for the file style.
